NEXT.JS · TYPESCRIPT · LARAVEL
01 / THE BRIEF

More than a marketing site.

Websofy is a full corporate website with a content management backend. The frontend is Next.js with TypeScript and Tailwind CSS; the backend is Laravel, PHP and MySQL.

The goal was to let non-developers keep the site fresh, while keeping the frontend fast, structured and search-friendly.

Next.jsTypeScriptTailwind CSSLaravelPHPMySQL
“Good SEO starts in the CMS, not after launch.”
THE BUILD PRINCIPLE
02 / WHAT I BUILT

Frontend, CMS and SEO.

The public site covers the full story of a modern services company, and the admin side controls what goes on it.

  • Frontend sections: Hero, About, What We Offer, Tech Pipeline, Industries, Why Choose Us, Vision & Mission, Partners, Testimonials, Clients, Case Studies, Development Process, FAQ, Contact, CTA, Footer and Blog.
  • Role-based CMS with Super Admin, Admin, HR, Content Manager and Blog Editor roles.
  • Dynamic content for solutions, packages, case studies, blogs, consultations and images.
  • SEO management per page: URL, H1, meta title, meta description, keywords, JSON-LD and FAQs.
Admin edits→Laravel API→MySQL→Next.js page→SEO-ready output
WHAT THIS PROJECT BROUGHT TOGETHER

Next.js frontend

Typed, componentised sections styled with Tailwind.

Laravel CMS

Roles, dynamic content and consultation handling.

SEO tooling

Editable meta, JSON-LD and FAQ data for every page.

03 / THE TAKEAWAY

What it
taught me.

Giving editors proper SEO fields turned the site into something a team can run on its own. It sharpened how I design admin panels: roles first, content second.
